# Sirach Chapter 48 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 48 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**48:1** Then Elijah arose like fire, and his word burned like a torch.

**48:2** He brought famine upon them, and by his zeal he reduced their number.

**48:3** By the word of the Lord he shut up the heavens, and also three times called down fire.

**48:4** How glorious you are, O Elijah, in your wondrous deeds! Who has the right to glory as you do?

**48:5** You who raised a dead man from death, from Hades, by the word of the Most High;

**48:6** who brought kings down to ruin and honored men from their beds;

**48:7** who heard rebuke at Sinai and judgments of vengeance at Horeb;

**48:8** who anointed kings to execute vengeance and prophets as your successors;

**48:9** who were taken up in a whirlwind of fire in a chariot with fiery horses;

**48:10** who are appointed for the times to calm wrath before it burns hot, to turn the heart of the father to his son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.

**48:11** Blessed are those who saw you, and those who have fallen asleep in love; for we too shall surely live.

**48:12** Elijah was enveloped in the whirlwind, and Elisha was filled with his spirit; throughout his life he was not shaken by any ruler and no one brought him under subjection.

**48:13** Nothing was too great for him, and even in death his body prophesied.

**48:14** In his lifetime he performed wonders, and at his death his deeds were marvelous.

**48:15** Despite all this the people did not repent, and they did not turn from their sins, until they were carried off as plunder from their land and were scattered over all the earth.

**48:16** Only a small remnant of people was left, and a ruler from the house of David. Some of them did what was pleasing to God, but others multiplied sins greatly.

**48:17** Hezekiah fortified his city and brought water into its midst; with iron tools he tunneled through solid rock and built cisterns for the water.

**48:18** In his days Sennacherib invaded and sent Rabshakeh and withdrew; he raised his hand against Zion and made great boasts in his arrogance.

**48:19** Then their hearts and hands trembled, and they were in pain like women in labor.

**48:20** But they called upon the merciful Lord, spreading out their hands toward him; and the Holy One quickly heard them out of heaven and delivered them through Isaiah.

**48:21** He struck the Assyrian camp, and his angel annihilated them.

**48:22** For Hezekiah did what was right and walked steadfastly in the ways of David his father, as commanded by Isaiah the prophet, who was great and trustworthy in his vision.

**48:23** In his days the sun moved backward, and he extended the life of the king.

**48:24** By a great spirit he saw the end of things, and he comforted those who mourned in Zion.

**48:25** He revealed what was to come to the end of time, and hidden things before they came to pass.
